articles.title: The Pre-Dawn USPTO Filing Window
articles.content:
近日，我在分析美国专利商标局（USPTO）的申请提交时间时发现，大部分申请集中在标准美国工作周内，但也有大量申请在非工作时间提交。例如，2025年5月至6月期间，约有1,300份新专利申请在东部时间凌晨3点至5点提交。根据数据显示，其中约三分之二来自东亚地区。中国贡献了26%的凌晨申请量，台湾19%，日本15%，韩国6%，另外还有一部分来自德国和以色列。

当美国弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市（USPTO总部所在地）的时间是凌晨4点时，台北和上海是下午4点，东京和首尔是下午5点，法兰克福和特拉维夫则是中午时分。这意味着这些国家的申请人正在按照当地的正常工作时间提交申请，而这些申请恰好在美国早上太阳升起之前到达。

然而，这引发了一个问题：谁在向USPTO提交申请？因为该局要求必须由美国专利从业者提交。直观的猜测可能是美国律师或代理人在夜深人静时工作，但我的调查结果并非如此。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

I was recently looking at timing of USPTO filings. The vast majority come in during the standard US work week, but a substantial number are submitted during off-hours.  For example, during May and June 2025 about 1,300 new patent applications arrived at the USPTO between 3 and 5 a.m. Eastern.  As the chart shows below, about two thirds of these came from East Asia. China accounted for 26% of that pre-dawn volume, Taiwan 19%, Japan 15%, and Korea 6%, with a second cluster out of Germany and Israel.

When it is 4 a.m. in Alexandria Virginia (USPTO HQ), it is 4 p.m. in Taipei and Shanghai, 5 p.m. in Tokyo and Seoul, and mid-morning in Frankfurt and Tel Aviv.  These are people working ordinary hours on their own clocks whose submissions happen to land in Virginia before sunrise.

But then that begs the question of who is actually submitting to the USPTO - since the Office requires a U.S. patent practitioner.  The natural assumption might be that a U.S. attorney or agent of record is burning the midnight oil - that is not what I found.

articles.title: Before the Sensor: Filter Ordering and Self-Collision in Amsted Rail v. Squires
articles.content:
联邦巡回法院维持了对安美德铁路公司（Amsted Rail）铁路车辆监控专利的索赔取消，同时否决了该公司提出的替换索赔请求。案件编号为2025-1063（联邦巡回法院2026年7月24日裁定，非判例力），涉及美国专利号10,137,915，该专利涵盖安装在货运车辆上的传感器节点和无线电设备，用于监测车辆脱轨、轮胎损坏和轴承过热等情况。索赔1中提及：

（b）一个或多个传感器……用于测量车辆的加速度；（c）一个或多个滤波器，用于过滤至少部分加速度……

安美德公司认为这两个要素必须按顺序操作：先测量，后过滤。但法院判定，除非语言逻辑或语法要求，或专利说明书将顺序作为发明的一部分，否则索赔并不要求要素按顺序运行。因此，这一解释为相关先前技术被认定无效开辟了道路。两起上诉均于6月1日进行辩论，本案与另一起涉及安美德两项专利的伴随案件，由同一法官面板于6月3日以单词“Rule 36”判决处理。

在索赔解释上，安美德公司依赖的是限定冠词：“第1索赔中的滤波器过滤‘该加速度’”，认为其指代的是传感器测量的加速度。然而，专利审查局将“该加速度”理解为包括车辆的物理运动，而不仅仅是信号本身，法院采纳了这一观点。据此解释，防止不需要的频率到达加速度计的硅垫也属于过滤加速度的范畴，符合第1索赔的表述。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The Federal Circuit has affirmed the cancellation of claims in Amsted Rail's railcar monitoring patent, along with the Board's refusal to let Amsted swap in substitute claims. Amsted Rail Co. v. Squires, No. 2025-1063 (Fed. Cir. July 24, 2026) (nonprecedential). U.S. Patent No. 10,137,915 covers sensor nodes and radios bolted onto freight cars to watch for derailments, damaged wheels, and overheating bearings. Claim 1 recites:

... (b) one or more sensors ... configured to measure accelerations of the railcar; and (c) one or more filters configured to filter at least a portion of the accelerations ...

Amsted argued the two elements as a sequence: measure first, filter second. But the panel held that the claim imposes no order, which opened the door to invalidating prior art. Both appeals were argued on June 1: this one and a companion covering two more Amsted patents, which the same panel disposed of on June 3 with a one word Rule 36 judgment.

Ordering. A claim does not require its elements to operate in sequence unless the language, as a matter of logic or grammar, demands it, or unless the specification makes the sequence part of the invention.

Amsted's hook was the definite article: claim 1's filters filter "the accelerations," which Amsted said refers back to the accelerations measured by the sensors. But the Board read "the accelerations" as including physical motion of the railcar rather than the signal alone, and the panel agreed. On that reading a silicone pad that keeps unwanted frequencies from ever reaching the accelerometer is filtering accelerations in the sense claim 1 uses.
